decisions.title: Adopt canonical context restoration for the ce-workflow context filter
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: use Pi 0.87.0's canonical provider-context handling with the existing ce-workflow context filter and no duplicate prompt/tool restoration code. Verified project fit: extensions/work-models.ts registers one context handler that returns a filtered messages array and never assigns session.agent.state.messages; its compaction path depends on built-in tool declarations surviving that filter. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.87.0 changelog, extension/session/compaction documentation, exported event types, runtime implementation, package metadata, and captured 0.85.1-to-0.87.0 artifact state that context handlers no longer receive system messages and Pi restores the prompt and tool state after they run. Benefit: filtered and compacted requests retain native tools without ce-workflow rebuilding host-owned transcript state. Cost/risk: ordinary host regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and keep the context hook message-only.

decisions.title: Keep new lifecycle, model, image, provider, SDK, and TUI behavior host-owned
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit Pi's actionable settle boundaries, canonical context edits, provider/model fixes, image limits, cache warming, SDK, and TUI lifecycle without a ce-workflow adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow uses public event registration, SessionManager reads, modelRegistry lookup, and explicit turn_end/agent_settled orchestration; it does not use the removed shouldStopAfterTurn option, construct exhaustive SessionEntry or ExtensionEvent switches, assign provider message state, register a custom provider, or own image resizing and editor rendering. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.86.0 through 0.87.0 changelog entries, linked public docs, exported types, runtime source, and captured artifact define these as host capabilities. Benefit: reliability and model/runtime improvements arrive from their owner without duplicating scheduling or transcript machinery. Cost/risk: ce-workflow keeps its coded lease and goal-continuation gates rather than speculatively migrating them to agent_before_settle. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local lifecycle or provider shim.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Remove retired completionGuard frontmatter
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 metadata and assertion cleanup. Bottom line: delete completionGuard from every ce-workflow agent because pi-subagents 0.70.1 removed the setting and now trusts process results plus explicit output and acceptance checks. Verified project fit: ten ce role files still declared completionGuard: false and two tests required the retired line, while direct role handoffs already pass acceptance level none because coded work-item gates own completion. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.70.1 changelog and current agent/tool-reference documentation remove completionGuard from supported frontmatter and describe explicit structured acceptance. Benefit: eliminates dead configuration and prevents stale tests from pinning an unsupported contract. Cost/risk: none beyond requiring the installed 0.70.1 semantics. Confidence: high. Recommendation: remove the retired field now.

decisions.title: Keep ce-workflow's coded acceptance and child capability boundaries
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 role metadata or settings change. Bottom line: do not add acceptanceRole: writer, defaultSubagentOnlyExtensions, or allowedAgents to ce roles without an uncoded launch that needs them. Verified project fit: directRoleHandoffParams explicitly disables plugin acceptance in favor of ce-workflow's reviewer, verification, lease, and finish gates; immutable verifiers explicitly disable ambient project context and skills and receive only four checkpoint tools; ordinary roles do not launch descendants. Verified upstream evidence: 0.70.0 and 0.70.1 document these settings as optional defaults and restrictions, and state that explicit acceptance overrides inferred writer gates. Benefit: avoids duplicate review gates and wider child extension loading. Cost/risk: direct ad-hoc invocation of a package agent gets lightweight attestation, which is outside the coded workflow contract. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain explicit per-launch acceptance and tools.

decisions.title: Inherit runtime routing, foreground launch, detach, watchdog, and status fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: take pi-subagents' model preference, host resolution, background settlement, detached visibility, supervisor wake, tool-budget, and status fixes without local copies. Verified project fit: ce-workflow launches through the supported RPC boundary with explicit run identity, async mode, attention controls, output routing, and recovery; it has no fallbackModels configuration and does not resolve the host SDK itself. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.67.0 through 0.70.1 changelog, current agent/workflow/tool docs, package metadata, and captured 0.66.0-to-0.70.1 artifact assign these behaviors to pi-subagents. Benefit: more reliable managed runs without parallel runtime code. Cost/risk: ordinary plugin regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local runtime adapter.

decisions.title: Package-owned private outcome events and compatibility fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit redacted ask outcome events, Kitty repeat/release filtering, and TypeBox-shim compatibility directly from pi-ask-user. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes ask_user through normal tool results and lifecycle hooks, has no ask:answered or ask:cancelled listener, does not set PI_ASK_USER_EMIT_FULL_EVENTS, and does not copy the plugin schema or overlay listener. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.15.0 README, package metadata, public schema, implementation diff, and captured 0.14.0-to-0.15.0 artifact document these surfaces; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: safer event privacy and more reliable prompts without a second owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local event adapter or full-event opt-in.

decisions.title: Open ask_user decision context by default
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 environment default. Bottom line: set PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED=true when ce-workflow loads so decision evidence is visible without Ctrl+E. Verified project fit: ce-workflow routinely supplies decision context for planning, approvals, and recovery; the extension-level default covers every ask_user call while preserving an explicit true or false user environment preference. Verified upstream evidence: pi-ask-user 0.15.0 reads PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED at call time and supports contextExpanded as the per-call override. Benefit: actors see the full message immediately. Cost/risk: large contexts consume more terminal space. Confidence: high. Recommendation: use expanded context as ce-workflow's default.

decisions.title: Package-owned session alias command and Unicode-safe Windows broker launch
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit the /alias command and UTF-16LE Windows hidden-launcher fix from pi-intercom without a ce-workflow adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow does not name sessions or spawn the intercom broker, keeps pi-intercom optional, uses list-cwd only for operator discovery, and already requires exact session IDs for trust-sensitive or ambiguous coordination. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.13.0 README, package metadata, implementation diff, public command/tool behavior, and captured 0.12.1-to-0.13.0 artifact document both changes; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: users can persist a peer-friendly session name and Windows installations with non-ASCII paths launch reliably, while transport ownership stays in the plugin. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code, docs, or naming convention.

decisions.title: Name ce-workflow role sessions through /alias
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 optional naming policy. Bottom line: do not add alias mutation to coded role launches. Verified project fit: managed subagents already carry stable run and child identity, while delayed supervisor guidance intentionally prefers exact session IDs when identity matters. Verified upstream evidence: 0.13.0 presents /alias as a user-facing current-session command, not a subagent routing requirement. Benefit: preserves collision-resistant run identity and avoids persistent name churn. Cost/risk: operators may still set friendly aliases manually for long-lived peer sessions. Confidence: high. Recommendation: reserve /alias for user-managed peers.

decisions.title: Inherit pi-goal recovery, stale-context, settings, and documentation fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: keep pi-goal 0.54.8 package-owned and make no ce-workflow compatibility adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's coexistence path only reads the canonical custom goal-state entry and sends public /goal pause and /goal resume commands; the installed persistence source still serializes data.goal under customType goal-state, and the public commands remain unchanged. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.54.8 README, managing-goals and settings references, package metadata, source, and captured 0.54.4-to-0.54.8 artifact show internal transient-stream classification, stale extension-context cancellation, menu/settings lifecycle, and documentation/build changes while preserving the coexistence surface. Benefit: pi-goal users receive safer recovery and lifecycle behavior without duplicate state ownership. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Adopt live diagnostics freshness and path-normalization fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: use pi-lens 4.2.1 for parent and reviewer live diagnostics without adding ce-workflow-side stale-result or path-casing logic. Verified project fit: ce-workflow guidance already requires source=lsp path probes when session findings are absent or stale and treats live diagnostics as parent/reviewer evidence; it does not cache or normalize lens findings itself. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 4.2.0 and 4.2.1 changelog, public tool schema, package metadata, and captured 4.1.4-to-4.2.1 artifact document carried-finding re-verification, explicit age labels, path normalization, silent-server warm-up, grouped delta rendering, and disposition-safe diagnostics. Benefit: fewer stale, orphaned, mis-grouped, and false-clean diagnostics. Cost/risk: ordinary plugin regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now through the existing public lens_diagnostics contract.
decisions.verification: lens_diagnostics source=lsp scope=paths on the changed TypeScript and JavaScript files; installed package metadata reports 4.2.1

decisions.title: Keep immutable checkpoint verifiers isolated from live pi-lens expansion
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 3 evidence-boundary change. Bottom line: do not grant analysisRoot, lens_diagnostics, project_report, or new language/tool capabilities to immutable checkpoint verifiers. Verified project fit: verifier claims are content-hash-bound to work_verifier_read/list/find/grep snapshots, while live pi-lens observes the mutable workspace and package-global configuration. Verified upstream evidence: pi-lens 4.2.x adds live Typst, explicit analysis roots, status controls, diagnostics re-verification, and analyzer/LSP fixes rather than immutable checkpoint semantics. Benefit: preserves deterministic evidence ownership while parent and reviewer paths inherit live improvements. Cost/risk: checkpoint verification remains text-bound. Confidence: high. Recommendation: keep the existing four-tool verifier allowlist.

decisions.title: Leave LSP servers, formatters, analyzers, UI status, and graph internals package-owned
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit pi-lens 4.2.x implementation fixes without ce-workflow adapters or settings. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes public lens tools but does not implement language classification, LSP warm-up, formatter policy, diagnostic disposition, cascade rendering, status widgets, or analyzer runners. Verified upstream evidence: the installed changelog and captured artifact assign these features and fixes to pi-lens. Benefit: diagnostics improve at their owner boundary. Cost/risk: ordinary plugin regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local implementation.
